questions.stem: Any substance which, when eaten and absorbed, nourishes the body is
questions.explanation: Food is any substance that nourishes the body after digestion and absorption.

questions.stem: The state of the body resulting from a diet lacking in, or with an excess of, one or more nutrients is
questions.explanation: Malnutrition covers both under-nutrition and over-nutrition.

questions.topic: Careers associated with Foods and Nutrition
questions.stem: A professional who plans special diets for patients in a hospital is a
questions.explanation: Dietitians plan therapeutic diets for patients.

questions.topic: Careers associated with Foods and Nutrition
questions.stem: A graduate who develops new food products and improves processing methods in a factory is a
questions.explanation: Food technologists apply science to processing and product development.

questions.stem: Which vitamin is needed to prevent scurvy?
questions.explanation: Lack of ascorbic acid (vitamin C) causes scurvy, with bleeding gums.

questions.stem: Which mineral element is needed for the formation of haemoglobin?
questions.explanation: Iron is part of haemoglobin; its lack causes anaemia.

questions.stem: A snack provides 10 g fat, 20 g carbohydrate and 5 g protein. Using 9, 4 and 4 kcal per gram respectively, its energy value is
Which group consists only of fat-soluble vitamins?
questions.explanation: Vitamins A, D, E and K dissolve in fat; B-group and C are water-soluble.

questions.stem: When biuret reagent is added to a food solution, a violet colour indicates the presence of
questions.explanation: The biuret test is positive for protein (peptide bonds).

questions.stem: Eating rice and beans together improves the quality of the protein in the meal because
options: both are rich in animal protein of high biological value
beans destroy the starch in rice
rice contains all essential amino acids
the amino acids lacking in one are supplied by the other
questions.explanation: This is protein complementation (supplementary value of proteins).

questions.stem: Goitre, a swelling in the neck, results from a deficiency of
questions.explanation: Iodine is needed by the thyroid gland; deficiency causes goitre.

questions.stem: Serving yellow jollof rice with green vegetables and red tomato garnish mainly follows the meal-planning rule of
questions.explanation: Varied colour makes meals attractive and appetising.

questions.stem: When planning meals for a family on a low income, the homemaker should
options: buy only imported foods from large supermarkets abroad
use cheaper sources of nutrients such as legumes
questions.explanation: Legumes, seasonal produce and careful buying stretch a small budget.

questions.stem: A pregnant woman needs extra folic acid in her diet mainly to
options: reduce her body weight before the baby is born
prevent birth defects in the baby
questions.explanation: Folic acid lowers the risk of neural tube defects and supports blood formation.

questions.stem: For the first six months of life, a baby should ideally be fed on
questions.explanation: Exclusive breastfeeding is recommended for six months.

questions.stem: Meals for an elderly person should generally be
options: high in fat, very spicy and served in large portions
large and eaten late at night
light, easily digested and lower in energy
questions.explanation: Older people need less energy and benefit from soft, easily digested, nutrient-rich meals.

questions.stem: A kitchen layout in which work surfaces run along two parallel walls is the
questions.explanation: A galley (corridor) kitchen has units facing each other on two walls.

questions.stem: Kitchen floors should be made of materials that are
questions.explanation: Non-slip, washable floors are safe and hygienic.

questions.stem: A pressure cooker cooks food faster than an ordinary pot because it
options: lowers the boiling point of water
raises the boiling point of water
questions.explanation: Higher pressure raises the boiling point, so food cooks at a higher temperature.

questions.stem: Wooden or silicone spoons should be used in non-stick pans in order to
options: make the food taste much better
questions.explanation: Metal tools scratch and damage the non-stick surface.

questions.stem: Which container should NOT be used in a microwave oven?
questions.explanation: Metal reflects microwaves and may cause sparking.

questions.stem: Water should never be used to put out a fire caused by
questions.explanation: Water conducts electricity and can cause electrocution; switch off the power and use CO2 or powder.

questions.stem: When washing up after a meal, which items should be washed first?
questions.explanation: Wash the least greasy and dirty items first: glassware, cutlery, crockery, then pots.

questions.stem: Bacteria that cause food poisoning multiply most rapidly in food kept
questions.explanation: The danger zone is warm temperatures where bacteria multiply fastest.

questions.stem: Which of the following fish is classified as an oily fish?
questions.explanation: Oily fish such as mackerel, sardine and herring have oil distributed in their flesh.

questions.stem: Rubbing unripe pawpaw on tough meat before cooking makes it tender because pawpaw contains the enzyme
questions.explanation: Papain breaks down meat proteins.

questions.stem: Periwinkles and oysters are classified as
questions.explanation: Shellfish with shells, like periwinkle and oyster, are molluscs; crabs and prawns are crustaceans.

questions.stem: In mayonnaise, egg yolk acts as an
options: emulsifier that keeps oil and vinegar mixed
colouring agent that makes the sauce yellow
questions.explanation: Lecithin in yolk stabilises the oil-in-vinegar emulsion.

questions.stem: Which part of a cereal grain is the main source of starch?
questions.explanation: The endosperm is the starchy store of the grain.

questions.stem: Parboiling rice before milling helps to
options: remove all the protein from the grain
retain B vitamins in the grain
questions.explanation: Parboiling drives B vitamins from the bran into the endosperm before milling.

questions.stem: The browning of bread when it is toasted is mainly due to
questions.explanation: Dry heat breaks starch into brown, sweet dextrins.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a leafy vegetable?
questions.explanation: Ugu (fluted pumpkin) leaves are a common leafy vegetable.

questions.stem: Adding baking soda to green vegetables during cooking should be avoided because it
questions.explanation: Alkali keeps the colour but destroys vitamin C and makes the texture mushy.

questions.stem: Slices of banana kept for a fruit salad turn brown on standing. This can be prevented by
options: leaving them uncovered in the hot sun
questions.explanation: Acid slows enzymic browning.

questions.stem: Akara and moin-moin are prepared from
questions.explanation: Both are made from ground cowpeas.

questions.stem: Dawadawa, a fermented food condiment, is produced from the seeds of the
questions.explanation: Dawadawa (iru) is made by fermenting locust bean seeds.

questions.stem: Red palm oil is a good source of
options: carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A
questions.explanation: Its red colour comes from carotenoids, precursors of vitamin A.

questions.stem: Margarine is produced from vegetable oils by
questions.explanation: Adding hydrogen to unsaturated oils hardens them.

questions.stem: Cocoyam must be well cooked mainly to destroy
options: excess vitamin C that sours the cooked tuber
calcium oxalate crystals that irritate the throat
questions.explanation: Calcium oxalate crystals cause itching and irritation if cocoyam is undercooked.

questions.stem: Gari is produced by
options: drying sliced cocoyam in the sun
questions.explanation: Cassava is grated, fermented, pressed and garified (fried).

questions.stem: A bulging (blown) can of food should be thrown away because it may contain
options: extra vitamins added by the manufacturer
questions.explanation: Bulging indicates microbial growth, possibly Clostridium botulinum.

questions.stem: Food poisoning traced to a food handler with an infected cut on the hand is most likely caused by
questions.explanation: Staphylococcus aureus lives on skin, cuts and in the nose.

questions.stem: Making jam preserves fruit mainly because the high concentration of
options: air in the jar kills bacteria
questions.explanation: Concentrated sugar draws water out of microbes by osmosis.

questions.stem: Sodium benzoate added to bottled fruit drinks acts as a
questions.explanation: Sodium benzoate inhibits yeasts and moulds.

questions.stem: The stock rotation rule which ensures that older food is used before newly bought food is
questions.explanation: FIFO prevents food from going past its use-by date.

questions.stem: Dry foods such as flour and rice should be stored in
options: the freezer section of the refrigerator
airtight containers in a cool dry place
questions.explanation: Airtight, cool, dry storage keeps out pests and moisture.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a reason for cooking food?
options: To make it safe by destroying germs
To make it harder for the body to digest
questions.explanation: Cooking kills micro-organisms, improves digestibility and flavour.

questions.stem: When sugar is heated until it melts and turns brown, the process is
questions.explanation: Caramelisation is the browning of sugar by heat.

questions.stem: Moin-moin wrapped in leaves and cooked over boiling water in a covered pot is cooked by
questions.explanation: Food cooked by steam from boiling water is steamed.

questions.stem: Which method of cooking best retains water-soluble vitamins in vegetables?
questions.explanation: Steaming avoids contact with water, so fewer vitamins leach out.

questions.stem: Heat travels through soup in a pot by the movement of the liquid itself. This is
questions.explanation: Warm liquid rises and cooler liquid sinks, forming convection currents.

questions.stem: Toasting bread in front of a glowing electric element transfers heat mainly by
questions.explanation: Radiant heat travels directly from the hot element to the food.

questions.stem: The term 'garnish' refers to
questions.explanation: Garnishes decorate savoury food; decorations are used on sweet dishes.

questions.stem: Soaking meat in a mixture of oil, acid and spices before cooking is called
questions.explanation: A marinade tenderises and flavours meat.

questions.stem: A dish topped with cheese or breadcrumbs and browned under a grill is served
questions.explanation: Au gratin means with a browned crust of cheese or crumbs.

questions.stem: A mixture of equal amounts of melted fat and flour cooked together as the base for sauces is a
questions.explanation: A roux thickens white sauces and gravies.

questions.stem: Baking powder releases carbon dioxide because it contains
options: whisked egg white and caster sugar
bicarbonate of soda and an acid
questions.explanation: Sodium bicarbonate reacts with an acid such as cream of tartar when moistened and heated.

questions.stem: A cake sinks in the middle after baking. A likely cause is
questions.explanation: Excess raising agent overstretches the mixture, which then collapses.

questions.stem: Pancakes are made from a
questions.explanation: A thin pouring batter is used for pancakes.

questions.stem: Éclairs and cream puffs are made from
questions.explanation: Choux pastry is a cooked paste that puffs up with steam.

questions.stem: Baking a pastry case without its filling, using greaseproof paper and dried beans, is
questions.explanation: Baking blind sets the pastry before the filling is added.

questions.stem: Kneading a bread dough mainly helps to
questions.explanation: Kneading stretches gluten, giving bread its structure.

questions.stem: Allowing shaped bread dough to rise a second time before baking is called
questions.explanation: Proving is the final rising of shaped dough.

questions.stem: Almond paste (marzipan) is applied to a fruit cake before royal icing in order to
questions.explanation: Marzipan seals crumbs and gives a smooth base for icing.

questions.stem: Palm wine is classified as
questions.explanation: Fermented palm sap contains alcohol.

questions.stem: Beverages are important in the diet mainly because they
questions.explanation: Beverages provide fluid and, in some cases, nutrients and energy.

questions.stem: When making cocoa, the powder is first mixed to a paste with a little cold milk in order to
questions.explanation: Blending to a paste first separates starch grains so they do not form lumps.

questions.stem: One advantage of convenience foods is that they
options: are always cheaper than fresh food
questions.explanation: Convenience foods save time and labour.

questions.stem: Shepherd's pie is a rechauffé dish made from cooked minced meat topped with
questions.explanation: Leftover minced meat is covered with mashed potato and browned.

questions.stem: Dishes prepared for the New Yam festival in many Igbo communities feature mainly
questions.explanation: The festival celebrates the yam harvest, so yam dishes such as roasted yam and yam pottage are central.

questions.stem: The letters R.S.V.P. on an invitation card request the guest to
questions.explanation: RSVP is French for 'please reply'.

questions.stem: In laying a cover, the side plate is placed
options: on the right of the knife
on the left of the forks
in the centre of the cover
questions.explanation: The side plate goes on the left, beyond the forks.

questions.stem: Food plated in the kitchen and carried to each guest ready to eat is
questions.explanation: American (plated) service presents ready plated food.

questions.topic: Research into Local Dishes and Drinks
questions.stem: Burukutu, a traditional fermented drink, is brewed mainly from
questions.explanation: Burukutu is a sorghum beer of northern Nigeria.

questions.stem: In a class experiment, iodine solution turns blue-black when added to a food sample. This shows the presence of
questions.explanation: Iodine gives a blue-black colour with starch.

questions.stem: Checking the expiry date on a can of tomato paste before buying is an application of
questions.explanation: Consumer education teaches people to examine labels and buy wisely.

questions.stem: A family's monthly food budget is N80,000. If 15% is spent on protein foods, the amount is
Rice is sold at N900 for a 500 g pack or N1,700 for a 1 kg pack. Which statement is correct?
options: The 500 g pack is cheaper per kilogram
The 1 kg pack is cheaper per kilogram
Both cost the same per kilogram
The 500 g pack costs N1,700 per kilogram
The 1 kg pack costs N1,800 per kilogram
questions.explanation: Two 500 g packs cost N1,800 per kg, versus N1,700 for the 1 kg pack.

questions.topic: Setting up and Managing a Catering Enterprise
questions.stem: Before opening a restaurant in Nigeria, the owner should register the business with the
questions.explanation: Businesses are registered with the CAC.

questions.stem: Which packaging material is biodegradable?
questions.explanation: Paper breaks down naturally; plastics and polystyrene persist.

questions.stem:
(a) Name two sources and one deficiency disease each for (i) vitamin D (ii) iron. [6 marks]
(b) State four functions of water in the body. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: Vitamin D sources: sunlight on skin, fish liver oil, egg yolk, fortified milk (any two)
1 mark: Vitamin D deficiency: rickets (osteomalacia in adults)
1 mark: Second source of vitamin D correctly named
1 mark: Iron sources: liver, red meat, green leafy vegetables, beans (any two)
1 mark: Iron deficiency: anaemia
1 mark: Second source of iron correctly named
1 mark: Medium of transport of nutrients and wastes
1 mark: Regulates body temperature through sweat
1 mark: Aids digestion and excretion
1 mark: Lubricates joints and is part of body fluids
questions.explanation: Vitamin D comes from sunlight, fish oils and eggs; lack causes rickets. Iron comes from liver, meat and leafy greens; lack causes anaemia. Water transports, cools, aids digestion and lubricates.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain why each of the following groups has special nutritional needs: (i) pregnant women (ii) adolescents. [4 marks]
(b) Plan a one-day menu suitable for a pregnant woman. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Pregnant women: extra protein, iron, folic acid and calcium for the growing baby and blood volume
2 marks: Adolescents: rapid growth spurt and activity need more energy, protein, calcium and iron
2 marks: Breakfast that is balanced, e.g. pap with milk and akara, fruit
2 marks: Lunch that is balanced, e.g. rice, vegetable soup with fish, orange
2 marks: Dinner that is balanced and light, e.g. yam porridge with leafy vegetables and egg; adequate fluids
questions.explanation: Pregnant women need more protein, iron, folate and calcium; adolescents need more of everything for growth. A good menu spreads protein, vegetables, fruit and dairy across three balanced meals.

questions.stem:
(a) Classify kitchen equipment into two groups, giving two examples of each. [4 marks]
(b) State three guidelines for the care of a refrigerator. [3 marks]
(c) Give three points to consider when buying kitchen equipment. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Large equipment, e.g. cooker, refrigerator, freezer
2 marks: Small equipment, e.g. knives, pots, blender, sieve
1 mark: Defrost regularly and clean with warm water and bicarbonate of soda
1 mark: Cover food and do not put hot food inside
1 mark: Avoid opening the door unnecessarily; keep away from heat
1 mark: Cost and family budget
1 mark: Durability, quality and ease of cleaning
1 mark: Size, available space, safety and after-sales service
questions.explanation: Equipment is large (cooker, fridge) or small (knives, blender). Fridges need defrosting, covered cool food and minimal door opening. Buyers should weigh cost, quality, size and after-sales service.

questions.stem:
(a) Name four agents of food spoilage. [4 marks]
(b) State three signs that fresh meat has gone bad. [3 marks]
(c) Give three ways of preventing food poisoning at home. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: Bacteria
1 mark: Moulds
1 mark: Yeasts
1 mark: Enzymes or pests such as rodents and insects
1 mark: Unpleasant smell
1 mark: Slimy or sticky surface
1 mark: Greenish or dull grey colour
1 mark: Wash hands and keep kitchen clean
1 mark: Cook food thoroughly and serve it hot
1 mark: Store food at safe temperatures and cover it
questions.explanation: Spoilage is caused by bacteria, moulds, yeasts, enzymes and pests. Bad meat smells, feels slimy and discolours. Hygiene, thorough cooking and proper storage prevent food poisoning.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the following methods of cooking, giving one Nigerian food cooked by each: (i) steaming (ii) roasting (iii) deep fat frying. [6 marks]
(b) State two advantages and two disadvantages of frying. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Steaming: cooking in steam from boiling water, e.g. moin-moin
2 marks: Roasting: cooking with dry heat in an oven or over open fire, e.g. roast plantain (boli), suya
2 marks: Deep frying: food immersed in hot fat, e.g. akara, puff-puff
1 mark: Advantage: quick method of cooking
1 mark: Advantage: adds flavour, colour and crispness
1 mark: Disadvantage: adds fat and energy to food, unsuitable for some diets
1 mark: Disadvantage: risk of fire and burns; food can be greasy
questions.explanation: Steaming uses steam (moin-moin), roasting uses dry heat (boli, suya), deep frying immerses food in oil (akara). Frying is fast and tasty but fattening and risky.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the function of each of the following ingredients in bread making: (i) yeast (ii) strong flour (iii) salt (iv) sugar. [4 marks]
(b) Outline the stages in making bread rolls after the dough has been mixed. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: Yeast ferments sugar to produce carbon dioxide that raises the dough
1 mark: Strong flour has high gluten that forms an elastic network to hold the gas
1 mark: Salt gives flavour and strengthens gluten, controlling yeast activity
1 mark: Sugar provides food for the yeast and helps browning
1 mark: Knead until smooth and elastic
1 mark: Leave covered in a warm place to rise until double in size
1 mark: Knock back to remove large air bubbles
1 mark: Divide and shape into rolls on a greased tray
1 mark: Prove until well risen
1 mark: Bake in a hot oven until brown and hollow-sounding
questions.explanation: Yeast raises, strong flour supplies gluten, salt flavours and controls, sugar feeds yeast. Then knead, rise, knock back, shape, prove and bake hot.

questions.stem:
(a) Classify beverages into four groups with one example each. [4 marks]
(b) Describe the preparation of zobo drink. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: Stimulating, e.g. tea, coffee
1 mark: Nourishing, e.g. milk, cocoa drink, kunu
1 mark: Refreshing, e.g. fruit juice, zobo
1 mark: Alcoholic, e.g. palm wine, burukutu
1 mark: Pick over and wash dried roselle calyces
1 mark: Boil in water with flavourings such as ginger or pineapple peel
1 mark: Simmer for about 15 minutes, then allow to cool
1 mark: Strain through a clean sieve or cloth
1 mark: Sweeten to taste and add fruit juice if desired
1 mark: Bottle hygienically and chill; serve cold
questions.explanation: Beverages are stimulating, nourishing, refreshing or alcoholic. Zobo: wash roselle calyces, boil with ginger, simmer, cool, strain, sweeten, bottle and chill.

questions.stem:
(a) State four rules for laying a table for a formal dinner. [4 marks]
(b) State six rules of good table manners. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: Use a clean, well-ironed table cloth
1 mark: Lay cutlery in order of use from the outside inwards, knives right, forks left
1 mark: Place the glass at the tip of the knife and the side plate on the left
1 mark: Place napkins, cruet and centrepiece neatly; covers evenly spaced
1 mark: Wash hands before eating
1 mark: Sit upright and do not put elbows on the table
1 mark: Chew with the mouth closed and do not talk with food in the mouth
1 mark: Do not reach across others; ask for items to be passed
1 mark: Use cutlery correctly and lay knife and fork together when finished
1 mark: Wait for the host to start; excuse yourself politely when leaving
questions.explanation: Formal tables need a clean cloth, cutlery from outside in, glass above the knife and side plate on the left. Good manners include clean hands, upright posture, closed-mouth chewing, not reaching and correct cutlery use.

questions.stem:
(a) State four rules for using leftover foods. [4 marks]
(b) Suggest one dish that can be made from each of the following leftovers: (i) cooked rice (ii) boiled yam (iii) stale bread. [3 marks]
(c) Give three advantages of using leftover foods. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: Reheat thoroughly, only once
1 mark: Use leftovers quickly, within a day, and store them covered in a refrigerator
1 mark: Add fresh ingredients to improve flavour and nutritive value
1 mark: Season well and serve attractively
1 mark: Cooked rice: fried rice or rice balls
1 mark: Boiled yam: yam balls or yam pottage
1 mark: Stale bread: bread pudding, croutons or breadcrumbs
1 mark: Reduces food waste
1 mark: Saves money
1 mark: Saves time and gives variety to meals
questions.explanation: Leftovers must be stored cold, used quickly and reheated thoroughly once, with fresh additions. Rice becomes fried rice, yam becomes yam balls, bread becomes pudding. This saves waste, money and time.

questions.topic: Setting up and Managing a Catering Enterprise
questions.stem:
(a) State five factors to consider when setting up a small catering business. [5 marks]
(b) Explain five qualities of a good caterer. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: Capital and source of finance
1 mark: Location and target customers
1 mark: Equipment, premises and utilities
1 mark: Registration, permits and health certification
1 mark: Staff, menu, pricing and competition
1 mark: Hygienic in person and practice
1 mark: Honest and reliable/punctual
1 mark: Creative in menu planning and food presentation
1 mark: Good at costing and managing money
1 mark: Courteous with good communication and human relations
questions.explanation: A caterer must consider capital, location, equipment, registration, staff and pricing, and must be hygienic, honest, creative, financially careful and courteous.
